answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock tokens and build a history of useful work before its votes count, so a Sybil farm that spins up a thousand empty accounts reaches the summit of nothing — no stake, no track record, no weight. Newcomers start in an umber zone of limited trust and climb only by delivering verifiable results, while a saffron-flagged anomaly check catches clusters that act in lockstep and slashes their stake, turning mass forgery into a money-losing grind.
